keywords: armyworm maize caterpillars sawdust kaduna
content: According to NAERLS and IITA, Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) causes sawdust-like droppings in maize whorls. For low-cost local control, do not use cassava flour. Mix neem seed extract or garlic with water and a drop of local soap, then spray directly into the whorl. For severe outbreaks, use Emamectin benzoate.

keywords: yam leaves yellow green veins benue
content: Yellowing yam leaves with green veins indicates Yam Mosaic Virus (YMV), which is spread by aphids. There is no chemical cure for viral infections. You must uproot and destroy the infected plants to save the rest of the farm. Next season, ensure you buy certified, virus-free seed yams or minisetts.

keywords: cassava sandy soil south east plant ridge
content: Cassava is propagated using stem cuttings, never tubers. Cut healthy stems into 20-25cm lengths. For sandy soils in the South East, use drought-resistant varieties like TMS 30572 or TME 419. Plant cuttings at a 45-degree angle. Space ridges 1 metre apart, and plant stems 1 metre apart (1m x 1m spacing) for a target of 10,000 plants per hectare.

keywords: maize variety seed drought striga sammaz yield
content: Use recommended drought and Striga-tolerant maize varieties like Sammaz 17 to Sammaz 39 depending on your ecology. Sammaz 21 is highly tolerant to Striga, while Sammaz 22 to 25 are drought-tolerant for the Northern Guinea Savannah.

keywords: maize plant seed spacing rate hole thin hectare
content: Plant maize at a spacing of 75cm x 50cm (two plants per stand) or 75cm x 25cm (one plant per stand). Use 15 to 20kg of seeds per hectare. Plant 3 seeds per hole and thin to two plants per stand at 1 to 2 weeks after germination.

keywords: maize fertilizer npk urea apply dose weeks nutrient
content: Apply fertilizer in two split doses. Apply the first dose (NPK 15-15-15) at planting or within the first week. Apply the second dose (Urea) between 4 and 5 weeks after planting. Apply in small quantities 5 to 8cm away from the plant and cover with soil to prevent nutrient loss.

keywords: maize weed striga parasite herbicide atrazine paraquat control
content: Control weeds in maize using pre-emergence herbicides like Paraquat mixed with Atrazine within three days after planting. For Striga (a parasitic weed), use an integrated approach: rotate with soybeans, plant Striga-tolerant varieties, and apply recommended fertilizer rates.

keywords: maize stem borer insect pest cypermethrin damage spray
content: To control stem borers in maize, apply a single properly timed spray of 100-120mls of Cypermethrin 10 EC or 80-100 mls of lamdacyhalothrin 2.5EC.

keywords: maize store weevil pest grain actellic phostoxin dry moisture
content: Dry harvested maize to 10-12% moisture content. To control grain weevils, treat stored grains with Actellic (primophos methyl) 2% dust at 500g per ton. For large sack storage, use 4 to 6 Phostoxin tablets per ton under an air-tight tarpaulin (ensure it is away from living rooms as fumes are poisonous).

keywords: cassava plant stem cutting node slanting horizontal spacing
content: For cassava propagation, use 6-12 month old healthy stems. Cut into lengths with 5-7 nodes. Store stems under shade for 4-10 days before planting to speed sprouting. Plant horizontally or slanting at a 45-degree angle, not vertically. Space at 1m x 1m.

keywords: cassava fertilizer npk yield application ring
content: Cassava responds well to fertilizer in poor soils. Apply 400kg/ha (8 bags) of NPK 15:15:15. Apply in a ring form around the base of the plant. You can also use 2-3 tons of poultry or cattle manure per hectare.

keywords: cassava termite white ant stem cutting dip chloropyrifos
content: To control termites and white ants in cassava, dip the stem cuttings in a solution of chloropyrifos (2ml per 1 litre of water) for 5 minutes and allow to dry before planting. This also protects against cassava mealy bugs.

keywords: cassava mosaic disease virus whitefly leaf distortion yellow
content: African Cassava Mosaic Disease is spread by whiteflies causing leaf distortion and vein clearing. There is no chemical cure. Use resistant varieties (like TME 419 or TMS 30572), uproot and burn infected plants.

keywords: cassava tuber harvest spoil store water moist processing
content: Fresh cassava tubers contain 70% water and spoil within 3-4 days of harvest. If you cannot process immediately, cover roots with jute bags and sprinkle with water to keep moist, but process within 4 days to avoid black streaks.

keywords: teak root rot tree yellow fall leaf stump rigidoporus lignosus
content: Root rot in Teak (Tectona grandis) is caused by Rigidoporus lignosus fungus living on old stumps. Leaves turn yellow and fall early. Control by removing old stumps, planting leguminous cover crops like Pueraria, or applying 2% tillex solution to the base.

keywords: nursery seedling damp pine eucalyptus die collapse water
content: Damping-off disease causes sudden collapse and death of pine and eucalyptus seedlings in the nursery. It is caused by Pythium or Fusarium fungi. Prevent it by avoiding over-watering, ensuring well-drained soil mixtures, and using 50% light shade.

keywords: iroko gall mahogany borer insect pest forest tree
content: For forest trees, the Iroko gall bug (Phytolyma lata) and Mahogany shoot borer (Hypsipyla robusta) are major pests. Avoid monocropping (single species plantations) and mix forest tree species to reduce pest outbreaks.

keywords: rice seed prime soak germination sprout apron star
content: Treat rice seeds with Apron Star 50 DS (10g per 4kg of seed). To hasten germination (seed priming), soak seeds in cold water for 12 hours, drain, and air-dry for 2 hours before sowing. This produces vigorous plants.

keywords: rice lowland swamp variety faro flood iron
content: For lowland or shallow swamp ecologies, use recommended varieties like FARO 44 (Sipi), FARO 51, FARO 52 (WITA 4), or FARO 60. For iron-toxic or water-logged areas, use FARO 15 or Suakoko 8.

keywords: rice upland variety faro nerica ofada
content: For upland rice farming, recommended high-yielding varieties include FARO 46 (ITA 150), FARO 55 (NERICA 1), FARO 56 (NERICA 2), and OFADA 1 or 2.

keywords: rice fertilizer lowland swamp npk broadcast urea panicle
content: For lowland rice, apply 80-30-30 NPK/ha. Apply half the Nitrogen and all Phosphorus and Potassium at planting. Broadcast the remaining Nitrogen (Urea) at 6-10 weeks after planting or at the panicle initiation stage.

keywords: rice weed striga parasite yellow stunted rotation
content: Striga is a parasitic weed causing yellowing and stunted growth in upland rice. Control it using an integrated approach: rotate rice with soybean or groundnut, apply organic manure, and weed early before the Striga produces seeds.

keywords: rice blast disease fungus diamond spot white panicle
content: Rice blast is a fungal disease showing diamond-shaped or spindle spots with gray centers on leaves. Prevent by avoiding excessive nitrogen fertilizer, burning diseased stubble, and spraying Mancozeb or Benlate fungicide.

keywords: rice storage paddy weevil phostoxin actellic dry moisture
content: Dry rice paddy slowly to 12-14% moisture on concrete or mats (not bare floors). To protect from weevils, treat with Actellic 2.5 dust or fumigate heavily infested paddy in air-tight bags using one Phostoxin tablet per 100kg bag.

keywords: onion dry season plant seed variety wuyan bijini nursery transplant
content: For dry season onion farming (Oct-Jan), use local varieties like Wuyan Bijini. Sow seeds in a nursery and transplant to the field when they are 6-8 weeks old.

keywords: onion fertilizer npk urea apply yield
content: Apply about 6 bags of NPK 15:15:15 and 1.5 bags of Urea per hectare (65kg N, 40kg P, 45kg K). Apply four weeks after transplanting.

keywords: onion water irrigation dry season stress furrow
content: Onions are highly sensitive to water stress. During the dry season, use furrow or basin irrigation every 5 to 7 days, applying about 350-550mm of water per season.

keywords: onion pest thrip maggot silver leaf downy mildew
content: Thrips cause a silvery appearance on onion leaves. Control with Endosulfan or Malathion. Downy mildew shows as a furry violet coating; control by spraying Ferbam or Zineb.

keywords: onion harvest cure store bulb neck fall bamboo grass
content: Harvest onions when the necks become soft and tops fall over, but before they dry completely. Cure them in the field. For low-cost storage, use bamboo or wood stacks stuffed with dry grass; they can store for up to 6 months.

keywords: local chicken free range house semi intensive perch nest litter
content: Adopt a semi-intensive system for local chickens. Build a well-ventilated house using mud or bamboo. Provide dry litter (wood shavings), perches placed 35cm apart, and laying nests (25x30x35cm) for egg collection.

keywords: local chicken feed supplement range scavenge grain ash
content: Free-range chickens pick up 60% of their diet (insects/greens) during the rainy season. Supplement their diet with 45-60g of feed daily using a mix of maize, offals, bone ash, and wood ash.

keywords: local chicken disease newcastle twist neck diarrhea red eye vaccinate
content: Newcastle disease is the biggest killer of local chickens (symptoms: twisting neck, red eyes, diarrhea). Since treatment is ineffective, prevention through vaccination (like thermostable NDV vaccine) is mandatory.

keywords: local chicken parasite lice tick mite feather peck dust
content: External parasites (lice, mites, ticks) cause chickens to lose weight and peck their feathers. Control this by regularly dusting the birds with poultry dusting powder like Sevin or Asuntol.

keywords: tomato harvest store fresh refrigerate paper bag
content: Harvest tomatoes when fully ripe, or at 60-80% ripeness and ripen indoors in a paper bag (not plastic). Do not refrigerate fresh tomatoes as it causes rapid flavor loss.

keywords: tomato sun dry slice tray net galvanized moisture powder
content: To sun-dry tomatoes, cut into 0.5cm slices. Spread on non-galvanized trays (acid reacts with metal). Cover with mosquito netting, turn daily, and bring indoors at night to prevent moisture reabsorption.

keywords: tomato processing preserve jam paste sterilize bottle boil mould
content: To preserve tomato paste or jam, sterilize glass bottles by boiling for 5 minutes. In tomato jam, mould growth on the surface indicates that not enough sugar was added.

keywords: snail breed species giant marginata achatina mature stock
content: For snail farming in Nigeria, use giant species like Archachatina marginata or Achatina achatina. Select fully grown, large snails with strong shells that fill their shells. Do not mix different species in the same pen.

keywords: snail soil moisture environment temperature wind
content: Snails require damp, medium-light soil rich in humus and calcium (for shell formation). Avoid hard clay or loose sand. Protect the farm from strong winds to prevent dehydration, and keep temperatures between 10-23°C.

keywords: snail pen hutch trench fence stock density
content: Build outdoor pens (5x5m) with fences buried 0.4m deep to keep out predators. Alternative housing includes hutch boxes under shade trees or 50cm deep trench pens. Stock at a density of 15 to 25 mature snails per square metre to avoid overcrowding.

keywords: snail feed eat leaf fruit salt predator ant
content: Snails are nocturnal and eat up to 10 times their weight daily. Feed them green leaves (cocoyam, cassava), ripe fruits (pawpaw, mango), or poultry mash. Keep common salt away as it is poisonous. Protect from termites, soldier ants, and rats.

keywords: snail harvest store mature reproduce egg hatch
content: Snails take 12 to 24 months to mature and are ready for harvest when they reach about 200g. Harvest by hand at night or when wet. Store live harvested snails in sawdust or chipped maize husks for 6 to 8 weeks.

keywords: 2019 wet season performance flood rain constraint labour
content: The 2019 NAERLS Agricultural Performance survey noted that flooding, high labour costs, low farm mechanization, and insecurity were major constraints. Floods affected over 25 states, destroying at least 25% of crops in affected areas.

keywords: tractor mechanization extension e-wallet helpline
content: To combat low agricultural yields and extension shortages, the NAERLS 2019 report recommends Public-Private Partnerships for tractor hiring, expanding e-extension through the National Farmers Helpline Centre, and distributing subsidized inputs via an e-Wallet system.

keywords: security farm herder clash banditry livestock transformation
content: Insecurity, including banditry and herder-farmer clashes, severely constrained farming in 2019. The government's Livestock Transformation Plan (LTP) aims to transition pastoralists into intensive production clusters to resolve these conflicts.

keywords: 2025 wet season performance rain yield maize rice cassava
content: According to the 2025 NAERLS Agricultural Performance Survey, production of major crops like rice (9.3M MT), maize (11.4M MT), and cassava (65.3M MT) increased over 2024 levels, leading to a general drop in food commodity prices.

keywords: 2025 wet season climate rain dry spell constraint
content: In 2025, while the North-West and South-West experienced higher rainfall that enhanced production, irregular rainfall patterns, frequent dry spells, and soil erosion continued to constrain agricultural productivity.

keywords: 2025 policy recommendation dry season subsidy mechanization
content: The 2025 NAERLS report highly recommends institutionalizing a Dry Season survey, digitizing fertilizer subsidies for affordable access, and revolutionizing mechanization through Public-Private Partnerships and simple labour-saving devices.

keywords: beniseed sesame soil plant spacing guinea sudan sahel
content: Beniseed (sesame) thrives on well-drained loamy soils. Plant in March/April for the Guinea savanna, or June/July for the Sudan and Sahel savannas. Space seeds at 60x10cm on flat land or 75x15cm on ridges.

keywords: beniseed sesame seed rate thin plant lodge
content: Use a beniseed seed rate of 4kg/ha for drilling or 5kg/ha for broadcasting. Thin the plants at 3 weeks after planting to exactly 2 plants per stand to prevent the plants from growing excessively tall and lodging.

keywords: beniseed sesame pest insect moth bug disease leaf spot
content: Beniseed is heavily attacked by pod-sucking bugs and leaf-feeding moths; control them with insecticides like Decis or Karate. Prevent Cercospora leaf spot disease using fungicides like Benomyl or Thiram.

keywords: beniseed sesame harvest cut capsule yellow shatter
content: Harvest beniseed when 50% of the capsules turn from green to yellow. Do not uproot; cut stems with sickles and tie them in upright bundles on a tarpaulin to dry fully. This prevents seed loss through shattering on bare ground.

keywords: beniseed sesame process dehull oil extract roast
content: To process beniseed, dehull by soaking in a 3% salt solution for 17-18 hours. To extract oil locally, roast the dehulled seeds for 5-10 minutes at 180-210°C, mill into flour, add hot water, and press.

keywords: cocoa black pod disease rot phytophthora prune south west
content: Black Pod disease in cocoa, prevalent in the humid South West, is caused by Phytophthora fungi. Control it by frequently removing infected pods, pruning the canopy to improve air circulation, and applying recommended copper-based fungicides.

keywords: catfish aquaculture clarias gariepinus water change ph ammonia
content: For African Catfish (Clarias gariepinus) farming, maintaining water quality is critical. High ammonia levels cause fish to gasp at the surface. Change pond water regularly, maintain a pH between 6.5 and 8.5, and avoid overfeeding to prevent water toxicity.

keywords: yam propagation minisett nrcri seed multiplication tuber
content: To overcome the shortage of seed yams, use the Minisett Technique developed by NRCRI Umudike. Cut a healthy tuber into 25g pieces (minisetts) ensuring each piece has peel, treat with a mixture of wood ash and fungicide, and plant in a nursery or direct field ridges.
